notes.claim: The number e is a fixed constant like π, approximately 2.71828, so it is a number to work with rather than a variable.
A logarithm answers "what power?": the base 2 logarithm of 32 is 5 because 5 is the exponent applied to 2 to get 32.

sources.title: Euler Number (e) — Definition, Formula & Examples
sources.quote: e is a fixed constant like π . It always equals approximately 2.71828 and cannot be assigned a different value.

sources.title: 6.3 Logarithmic Functions - Algebra and Trigonometry 2e | OpenStax
sources.quote: For example, the base 2 logarithm of 32 is 5, because 5 is the exponent we must apply to 2 to get 32.
